key_catalyst: Long-end Treasury yields at multi-decade highs (30y >5.2%, 10y 4.737%) on hawkish Fed dissent and bear steepening, pressuring Nasdaq-100 growth valuations
reasoning: The long end of the Treasury curve is still escalating rather than stabilizing — the 30-year closed above 5.2% (a 19-year high) and the 10-year hit 4.737% (highest since January 2025) on a bear steepening driven by Fed-credibility and inflation concerns — which directly compresses the high-multiple growth names that dominate QQQ. Market response confirms the pressure is unabsorbed: 7/31 gapped up +1.61% pre-market but bled -0.60% through the session, the same fade-the-open pattern seen repeatedly over the past three weeks. On top of that, Apple's guidance shock is still generating fresh negative flow less than 24 hours old (JPMorgan target revision, warnings that the memory shortage will 'significantly worsen' September-quarter supply for ~64% of revenue), and that memory/chip constraint theme is now spilling into a broader chip-sector selloff with Meta dropping sharply after hours into 8/1.
